summary: SSE session rebind during auth refresh yields interleaved token fragments and truncated JSON finalization
description: Issue summary: Customer reports partially-formed JSON choices when a long-running SSE stream is interrupted by a short network break that triggers an auth token refresh on the client. Impact: downstream app JSON parsing fails (invalid JSON), causing NoteStream to drop user sessions and surface 500s. Initial report came from two customers on the same dedicated pool.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a long SSE generation request (sequence length > 1200 tokens) against dedicated endpoint using SDK v1.3.2.
2) Force a lightweight network interruption for ~2–5s (simulate client NAT bounce) while stream is mid-output.
3) Client SDK auto-refreshes bearer token and reconnects immediately to the same path; SDK attempts resume with a new session cookie and idempotency token.
4) Observe final stream at client: final JSON choice object is interleaved with stale fragments, missing trailing brackets, or duplicated closing punctuation.
5) Server logs show resumed session accepted but with mixed session IDs in routing logs (old sessionId + new token).
observed_behavior: - Client receives a stream with duplicated mid-tokens and a truncated final JSON object (parse error).
- Token-level traces show fragment replay from the previous connection concatenated with the resume stream, producing invalid composite output.
- No persistent CPU/GPU errors on serving nodes; errors correlate with connections routed through a specific edge proxy cluster (edge-proxy-a).
expected_behavior: - Resume should be idempotent: either return the uninterrupted, complete final JSON choice OR a clean fallback response indicating resume failure.
- No interleaving of fragments from different authentication sessions or session IDs.
logs: edge-proxy: connection-break detected -> rebind attempt -> new auth token issued (refresh endpoint /auth/refresh)
serving-runtime: accepted resume with sessionId: s-73a1 (trace shows previous session s-6c0b still has active KV references)
router: routed fragments with session tag s-6c0b then s-73a1 within same application-level stream window
comments: 2026-03-10 (Aisha Patel): Customer reports invalid JSON after reconnect; attached client SDK logs and sample of truncated JSON (included). Asked for immediate mitigation options.
2026-03-10 (Support): Escalated to SRE and Serving Runtime teams; prelim hypothesis: session rebind + auth refresh causing duplicate fragment replay. Requested router/edge logs.

2026-03-11 (Marco Chen - SRE): Found that edge-proxy-a will sometimes reuse upstream connection handles when new auth headers are presented quickly after a short break; possible header race when session affinity metadata is updated.

2026-03-12 (Eng - Serving Runtime): Noted KV cache still attached to old session id until GC window expires (30s). If resume binds to new session id before old KV is drained, fragments may be stitched incorrectly by downstream stitcher.

2026-03-13 (Support): Sent recommended temporary mitigations to customer: increase client reconnect-backoff to >= 6s OR disable immediate resume in SDK v1.3.2; customer applied backoff and reported reduced incidents.
2026-03-14 (Marco Chen): Creating follow-up INT ticket to change router semantics and to add session-cohort verification on resume path.
investigation_notes: - Reproduced internally using a scripted NAT-bounce; observed same truncated JSON when router reused upstream handle and the serving-runtime resumed with mixed session tags.

- Packet-level tcpdump on edge-proxy-a shows two distinct Authorization headers arriving within the same 250ms window for the same logical client; upstream connection metadata updated but not fully reconciled.

- Trace instrumentation shows resume path route() does not currently validate that the sessionId embedded in resume metadata matches active KV owner; stitcher will append fragments if provenance differs.
- Only observed on dedicated pools with router version 2.11.0 and edge-proxy-a; other edge clusters (edge-proxy-b) running 2.12.1 not affected.
- SDK behavior: v1.3.2 auto-resumes aggressively; v1.4.0-beta includes optional idempotency header 'X-Resume-Token' which can help avoid mixing fragments but is not yet GA.
resolution: Workaround applied: customer set client reconnect backoff to 6s which prevents immediate resume and avoids fragment interleaving. Engineering action items: 1) short-term: add session-cohort verification in router resume path to reject resumes until KV owner reconciliation completes (PR opened), 2) mid-term: edge-proxy fix to avoid handle reuse within 1s of auth header change, 3) SDK: ship opt-in idempotency header in stable release and recommend conservative resume defaults. Full rollout scheduled across dedicated pools after review.
next_steps: 1) INT-1583: Router resume cohort validation (owner: Marco Chen) — implement and run canary on us-east dedicated pool.
2) Edge-proxy team to harden handle reuse policy and release 2.12.2 to edge-proxy-a cluster.
3) Backport SDK idempotency header to stable v1.4.0 and publish migration notes to customers.
4) Communicate mitigation and ETA to NoteStream CS contact (Claire Moreno).
